short_description: Consumer-facing appearance trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal for a younger-looking facial-aging tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing appearance trait with workable raw-array support and a clearer interpretation boundary between inherited facial-aging tendency and the many non-genetic factors that affect how old someone looks day to day.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with a tendency toward younger-looking facial ageing, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: Facial aging is presented here as a cautious relative appearance signal related to a younger-looking facial-aging tendency, not as a direct estimate of current visible age, biological age, or future ageing outcome. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a deterministic readout of how old someone looks right now.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.
Facial-ageing appearance is shaped by many non-genetic factors, including sun exposure, smoking, sleep, stress, weight change, skincare, health, and photography conditions.
This trait should be interpreted as a cautious relative appearance tendency, not as a promise about current or future visible ageing.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
